source.author: verg
source.text: At Trivia Hippolytum secretis alma recondit sedibus et nymphae Egeriae nemorique relegat, solus ubi in silvis Italis ignobilis aevom exigeret versoque ubi nomine Virbius esset.
source.text_original: At Trivia Hippolytum secretis alma recondit / sedibus et nymphae Egeriae nemorique relegat, / solus ubi in silvis Italis ignobilis aevom / exigeret versoque ubi nomine Virbius esset.
source.text_english: But Trivia, kindly, hides Hippolytus in secluded abodes and sends him away to the nymph Egeria and to the grove, where alone in the Italian woods he would spend his obscure life, and where, with his name changed, he would be Virbius.

reuse.text: altera cum paene amatorem suum perdidisset, qui erat turbatis distractus equis, praestantissimum medicum Asclepium curando iuueni aduocauit eumque sanatum secretis alma recondit sedibus et nymphae Egeriae nemorique relegat, solus ubi in siluis Italis ignobilis aeuum exigeret uersoque ubi nomine Virbius esset.
reuse.text_original: altera cum paene amatorem suum perdidisset, qui erat turbatis distractus equis, praestantissimum medicum Asclepium curando iuueni aduocauit eumque sanatum secretis alma recondit sedibus et nymphae Egeriae nemorique relegat, solus ubi in siluis Italis ignobilis aeuum exigeret uersoque ubi nomine Virbius esset.
reuse.text_english: The second, after she had nearly lost her lover, who had been torn apart by the panicked horses, summoned the excellent physician Asclepius to treat the young man, and when he had been healed she hid him away in secret, nurturing chambers, and banished him to the nymph Egeria and the grove, where he was to spend his life unknown in the Italian woods and where, with his name changed, he would be Virbius.
